decisions.reason: The source explicitly applies the same length-only study to the Hero V, but a complete same-message MODIFY already records the adjustment, locked geometry, and removal of the obsolete reach-study key.
The source explicitly applies the same proportional length adjustment to the É accent, and that impact is already fully represented by its same-message MODIFY.
The source revises the shared terminal study controls and variants, but the existing same-message MODIFY already records those changes and removes the obsolete refinement-variants key.
The source changes only the V-system right-arm study and expressly keeps the surrounding architecture and proportions locked; it does not alter the E or L letterform requirements.
The length-only geometric study does not change the established hierarchy: the second V remains subordinate to the Hero V, with only its right arm extending above the E and L.
The source explicitly treats the finish as locked and does not change the selected Satin Reflection treatment or champagne-gold distribution.
Applying the identical length change to the Hero V and É accent preserves their existing exact peak-alignment rule rather than modifying it.
The right-arm length study does not change the E/L cap-height rule based on the second V's left arm.
The client states that spacing is locked, so the selected Balanced Flow kerning and cohesive-reading requirement remain unchanged.
The source provides design feedback but does not change the independent obligation to explain the rationale behind review rounds.
Extending the right arms along their existing lines does not alter the bottom-point baseline alignment of the two Vs with the E and L.
